chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and others from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
"There is no harm in the wage of the broker and the guide; he merely buys for the people day after day for a known amount. He is like the laborer."

key_terms.اَلدَّلاَّلِ: Guide or finder who leads parties to a deal
key_terms.اَلسِّمْسَارِ: Broker or agent who facilitates a transaction for a fee

ai.seo_question: Is the commission of a real estate broker or commercial agent permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith validates the commercial practice of brokerage by likening the broker’s role to that of a hired laborer (*ajir*) who receives a known wage for facilitating transactions. This ruling underscores the permissibility of intermediary services in Islamic finance, provided the compensation is fixed and transparent, reflecting the practical economic needs of the Shia community. It serves as a foundational text for modern Islamic commercial law regarding agency and commission-based earnings.
